newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WANCHOPE SCORES ON DEBUT AS UNITED CRASH AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WANCHOPE SCORES ON DEBUT AS UNITED CRASH AT HOME.

text.p: Costa Rica's Paulo Cesar Wanchope scored a stunning individual goal on his premier league debut as Derby upset Manchester United 3-2 at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Wanchope, who joined struggling Derby last month and has only just received his work permit, picked the ball up inside his own half and surged towards Peter Schmeichel's goal, shrugging off challenges before side-footing the ball home as four United defenders closed in.

His goal revived memories of another Latin American strike at the heart of an English defence -- Diego Maradona's wonderful second goal in Argentina's 2-1 defeat of England in the 1986 World Cup finals.
Wanchope's strike and Derby's victory threw the English championship wide open again.
United still lead the pack by three points from both Arsenal and Liverpool, but third-placed Liverpool can return to the top for the first time since January 29 if they beat Coventry on Sunday.
Liverpool meet United at Anfield in two week's time in what could prove a title decider.
Saturday's defeat will also dent United's confidence ahead of Wednesday's European Cup semifinal first leg at Borussia Dortmund.
Alex Ferguson's men are looking to become the first English side to lift Europe's premier trophy since Liverpool in 1984.
Wanchope set up Derby's first goal on 29 minutes, heading the ball down for Ashley Ward to spoon a shot over Schmeichel into the net.
The Costa Rican then doubled Derby's lead six minutes later with his individual effort to ensure United were booed off the pitch by their own fans at halftime with the score 2-0.
Eric Cantona pulled one back for the champions after the break but with 15 minutes left Dean Sturridge took advantage of a rare mistake by Schmeichel to restore Derby's lead.
Second half substitute Ole Gunnar Solskjaer gave United hope with a late goal but, despite relentless pressure, United failed to find an equaliser.
The defeat was United's fifth of the season in the league and their first at home since Chelsea beat them 2-1 on November 2.
The result broight Arsenal back into the title race, although they have played a match more than United and trail them by three points.
Arsene Wenger's side won 3-0 at Chelsea earlier with goals from England internationals Ian Wright and David Platt and Dutch striker Dennis Bergkamp.
England striker Alan Shearer scored on his return after a groin operation in February but his Newcastle side were held 1-1 by Sunderland in the big north-east derby.
Newcastle remained fourth, level on points with Aston Villa who came from behind to beat Everton 3-1.
At the bottom, Nottingham Forest slumped 3-1 at home to fellow strugglers Southampton. Forest stayed 18th out of 20, a point ahead of Southampton.
